data.heading: Puerto Varas, located in the scenic Lake District in Southern Chile.
paragraphs: The 2026 meeting of the International Society for Hantaviruses took place in Puerto Varas, located in the scenic Lake District in Southern Chile widely regarded as a gateway to Patagonia. The city sits at the foot of the iconic Osorno Volcano in southern Chile, providing a spectacular natural setting for scientific exchange and collaboration.

The conference brought together scientists and health professionals from around the world to share and discuss the latest advances across a broad range of topics, including viral epidemiology, ecology, virus-host interactions, pathogenesis, clinical aspects of disease, and the development of vaccines and therapeutics.

data.heading: An excellent platform for students, postdoctoral researchers, and established scientists.
paragraphs: The International Conference on Hantaviruses provided a platform for students, postdoctoral researchers, and established scientists to present their latest findings and engage with the international hantavirus research community. Leading experts delivered keynote lectures highlighting cutting-edge developments in hantavirus research.

data.heading: A meeting place shaped by lakes, volcanoes and southern landscapes.
International scientific direction and Chilean local organization.
A one-day workshop dedicated to Andes virus.
paragraphs: On November 5, the conference was followed by a one-day workshop dedicated to Andes virus, a pathogen of particular regional importance. Researchers, clinicians, and public health professionals discussed local epidemiology, clinical management, and the public health response to hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome.
The workshop fostered dialogue between the scientific community and public health stakeholders. Photographs from the workshop are included in the conference gallery.
